summary: Named 75 of 145 FUN_XXXX functions in wroot.exe via Ghidra annotations (SourceType.USER_DEFINED). Coverage skews toward the MS-C 5.x runtime (41 fns) and the windowing UI (14 fns), with smaller but high-value clusters in keyboard input, file I/O, boot/disk-prompt, overlay loading, and mouse. The remaining 70 functions are mostly small game-logic helpers whose purpose can't be confidently inferred from static analysis alone — they need either string-ref tracing through the overlays (where most game data lives) or dynamic context.
method: PyGhidra + Ghidra's headless DecompInterface. For each function we extracted: (a) string operands by mapping DGROUP-relative (0x1fd80 base) and CS-relative (0x10000 base) scalar operands back to the in-memory ASCII strings; (b) INT 21h/10h/13h/16h interrupt sites with reverse-walk to find AH/AL/AX load instructions; (c) outgoing CALL edges; (d) decompiled C for any function with INT or string evidence. Names were applied only when there was direct evidence (DOS-int subfunction code, distinctive string ref, or unambiguous library pattern like memcpy/strcpy/strlen).

findings.claim: 0x14072 is the MS-C 5.x/6.x process entry point _astart

evidence.details: MZ header CS:IP = 0000:4072. Function resizes program memory via INT 21 AH=4A, parses argv from PSP env at [0x2c], zero-fills BSS from 0x6be for 0x2498 words, calls FUN_42bd (_cinit stub) then FUN_41df (_main).

Called from crt_startup with parsed argv/argc. Initializes _osfile[0..2] (TTY flags for stdin/stdout/stderr) via FUN_4485 (INT 21 AH=44 ioctl). Calls FUN_44a5 (sbrk) for argv table. Calls FUN_132d (ovl_install_table) and FUN_42ab (atexit+exit).

findings.applied_name: crt_dos_close / lseek / unlink / rename / ioctl / pack_open_flags / free_block / alloc_block

evidence.details: Each function contains exactly one INT 21h, with a preceding MOV AH,N where N maps to the standard DOS API number (3E=close, 42=lseek, 41=unlink, 56=rename, 44=ioctl, 49=free, 48=alloc). CF-failure path stores errno-equivalent at [0x660]. This is the canonical MS-C INT 21h dispatch idiom.

findings.claim: 0x13e88 implements the C runtime's _open() with O_* flag conversion

evidence.details: Builds 0x3D00 (open) or 0x3C00 (create) control word from O_RDONLY/CREATE/TRUNC/APPEND-style flags in param_2. Dispatches via crt_dos_open_or_create. On success, runs ioctl to set TTY flag in handle table at [fd+0x6a4]. This is the canonical MS-C _open structure.

memcpy at 0x1387a uses the classic 16-bit word copy with 1-byte tail. strcpy at 0x1390e measures source length then REP MOVSW + tail. strcat at 0x138d7 walks dst to nul then appends src. strlen at 0x1400f counts to nul and returns offset.

Scans format string for '%'; on hit, parses flags +/-/space/#, width, precision, then indexes into a jump table at 0x3b5a using char position in the string 'LlhFNoxXudiscpneEfgG%G' (this exact 22-char dispatch string lives at file 0x3d45). All major format conversions present (%d/%s/%c/%f/%g/%x/%X/%o/%u/%p/%n with l/h/F width modifiers).

findings.claim: 0x10d26 is the disk-swap / game-data load orchestrator

evidence.details: References ALL of: 'WMAZE.OVR', 'INSERT SAVEGAME DISK', 'INSERT DISK (^)', 'INTO DRIVE ^', 'PRESS X', 'CREDITS.PIC', 'DISK.HDR', 'MSG.DBS', 'SCENARIO.DBS' — i.e. every file the game prompts the user to load. Composes a window via ui_window_create, builds the prompt message via boot_build_prompt_message, waits for ENTER via kbd_check_with_filter, then opens via crt_open. Heart of the floppy-juggling UX.

References all overlay names in order: WINIT, WBASE, WMAZE, WMELE, WPOPS, WMEXE, WTREA, WPCMK, WPCVW, WMNPC, WDOPT. These are the 11 .ovr files in original/. Called from crt_main_set_iostate during startup.

findings.claim: 0x133e9 + 0x134d5 are the compressed-asset loader and Huffman bit-stream decoder

evidence.details: Matches the project's prior reverse-engineering anchor: 'FUN_33e9 Huffman decompressor'. Inner function (0x134d5) does 8-bit-at-a-time fetch from a 0x1000-byte buffer at 0x400; refills via INT 21 AH=3F when SI passes 0x13ff; walks a tree table at 0x357b using bit-direction left/right via 0x8000 leaf-flag — textbook Huffman decoder.

kbd_check_with_filter uses INT 16 AH=01 (status) + INT 21 AH=07 (raw read no echo) and filters chars by category mask (digit-only / printable / arrows). Maps arrow scancodes K/H/M/P to 0x08/0x09/0x0a/0x0b for unified handling. Internal queue at 0x262b/0x262d/0x262c (count/char/scancode arrays of size 20).

Three independent streams; each does (state % q) * a + (state / q) * c with stream-specific (q,a,c) = (0xb1,0xab,-2)/(0xb0,0xac,-0x23)/(0xb2,0xaa,-0x3f); reseeds to positive via +0x763d/0x7663/0x7673. This is the textbook Wichmann-Hill 1982 RNG.

All UI functions go through a driver function-table at [0x1b8a..0x1bca] (10 slots); window structs are linked through a chain at [0x1bd2]. Each window has shape: { width, height, top, left, ?, flags, cursor_x, cursor_y, ..., border_flags[9..f], char/attr cells[]@+0x10 }. The blit (0x12b19) is the heaviest path at 1082 bytes; it dispatches each cell through the driver and is wrapped by lock/unlock calls to [0x1ba2]/[0x1ba6].

unresolved: 69 functions remain as FUN_XXXX. They cluster in the 0x10100-0x10c00 range (small UI helpers, mostly tiny wrappers around the windowing dispatch) and 0x11800-0x12500 (more boot-time helpers and what appear to be format/print helpers).

Game-logic functions (combat, dungeon stepping, character stats, NPC dialog) are NOT in wroot.exe — wroot is just the dispatcher/loader. Those subsystems live in the overlays (wmele.ovr=combat, wmaze.ovr=dungeon, wpcmk.ovr=character creation, wpcvw.ovr=character view, wmnpc.ovr=NPC, wpops.ovr=popups, wtrea.ovr=treasure, etc.). Naming those is the next major task and requires per-overlay passes since they share segment 0x1fd8 for DGROUP.

Many remaining small functions (e.g. 0x1011a's neighbors at 0x10100-0x10c00) appear to be window-system helpers but with no direct evidence beyond participating in the UI dispatch table. Naming them confidently needs traces from dynamic runs OR understanding the driver fn-table layout.
next_steps: Rename pass on the overlays (especially wmaze.ovr and wmele.ovr) where the actual game logic lives. Headless setup is identical; loader spec differs (BinaryLoader + Real Mode).

Type/struct-shape pass on wroot: the window struct at offset 0/1/2/3/5/6/7/8-f/10... has a fairly clear layout that could be annotated as a Ghidra struct, dramatically improving decompiler output across all UI fns.
The driver function table at [0x1b8a..0x1bca] needs its 10 slots named — this maps directly to the driver-binary (ega.drv/cga.drv/etc.) exports.

operational_notes.key_quirk: Ghidra's MzLoader places strings at byte addresses 0x202xx but actual operand values in the code are DGROUP-relative offsets (subtract 0x1fd80, not 0x20000) — used 0x20000-0x1fd80 = 0x280 byte offset between the two interpretations. Code-segment-relative refs (e.g. 'ega.drv' at file_off 0x211c) appear as scalar 0x211c in instructions; their actual address in ram is 0x1211c (CODE_0 base 0x10000).
